Modified assessment incorporating Financial Stability Report (FSR) insights: The statement remains hawkish. It highlights elevated inflation and signals “ongoing increases” in the policy rate alongside continued balance sheet runoff, while raising administered rates (IORB, ON RRP) that tighten via reserves and the term-structure channels. The FSR adds that Treasury market liquidity and market depth have been strained with elevated rate volatility and rising term premiums, and that vulnerabilities in nonbank finance (including outflows from high-yield and bank‑loan funds) and a cooling housing market could amplify the transmission of tighter financial conditions. These financial stability considerations make the restrictive stance more binding and raise downside growth risks beyond the contemporaneous hike. Offsetting this somewhat, the FSR notes banks are well capitalized and core funding is resilient, which tempers tail risks. Netting these, the tone is moderately negative, a bit more so once FSR‑flagged vulnerabilities are considered.
